Video Summary:
Habits protect against ADHD, but why are they so hard to build when you have ADHD? Dr. K breaks down the neuroscience of weaker frontal lobes and dysregulated dopamine versus a separate, relatively intact habit circuitry you can train directly. Video Summary
What’s the real impact of divorce on kids and how does it affect them into their adult lives? Dr. K breaks down why kids of divorce bounce back but rarely to the same baseline, with real effects on academics, self-concept, and social competence. Shielding kids from conflict can backfire and introduce “disenfranchised grief”—the idea that kids rarely get space to mourn their family the way they would mourn a death. Dr. K also covers how  financial strain and disrupted routines can lead to early substance use, and why children of divorce often show more insecure attachment and difficulty in relationships as adults.

snippet.title: Why Your Addictive Personality Ruins Hobbies
snippet.description:
Learn how Dr. K’s world-class coaching program helps you build lasting change: https://go.healthygamer.gg/4x7l2z8
Go deeper & accelerate your growth with HG Memberships: https://go.healthygamer.gg/4gEOMyw
Learn more from Dr. K in his Guide to Mental Health: https://go.healthygamer.gg/4cwzs4F
Watch w/ a free trial 👉 Deep Dive into Perception: https://go.healthygamer.gg/4ynaFsd

Video Summary
Can you really have an “addictive personality”? Dr. K breaks down the neuroscience behind an addictive personality, framing it as an imbalance between the ventral tegmental area (dopamine/pleasure drive), the amygdala (fear/avoidance drive), and the frontal lobes (willpower), where willpower is outgunned by both drives, rather than one specific substance being the problem. People with this pattern tend to cycle through intense, consuming interests (hobbies, relationships, substances), and the core problem is based in acting rashly in response to negative emotion (avoidance) or positive emotion (impulsive pursuit). He applies the Buddha's "two arrows" teaching, pain versus suffering, and the overlooked half, pleasure versus obsession, to explain why chasing pleasure as a fix for pain is often the real root of addiction. He's clear this isn't about avoiding real action, just not attaching obsession to the outcome.

Video Summary:
Why does being gifted come with a cost? Dr. K breaks down the link between high IQ and anxiety—the better your brain gets at predicting future problems, the more problems you start to see in front of you, increasing your anxiety because you can only solve so many of them. That gap is why gifted kids ruminate, develop shortcut habits instead of discipline, and why income actually drops off at the highest IQ levels. Dr. K also covers why ADHD and autism spectrum traits show up alongside giftedness, and how emotional intelligence can outperform raw IQ at work.

Dr. K explains that effective therapy must be far more than simply talking about your feelings.
